title: Partial Final Month in Noticed Termination Damages
content:
**Q. Under Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts, what rule governs months counted when the term ends in a partial month in noticed terminations?**

A. The months counted for a noticed termination depend on whether the term ends with a partial month and on the notice lead of the noticed termination, the calendar days from the termination notice date to the termination effective date: with a partial final month and a notice lead of 60 days or more, only the whole months are counted; with a partial final month and a shorter notice lead, the whole months plus 0.5 are counted; otherwise the months are counted in full, as twelve times the difference in years plus the difference in months between the termination effective date and the contract end date, the two dates then falling on the same day of the month.

## Questions answered

**When does the term end with a partial month?** When the day of the month of the contract end date differs from the day of the month of the termination effective date.

**What are the whole months?** Calendar months counted from the termination effective date to the contract end date, a month being complete on the same day of the month as the termination effective date.

**How is the notice lead counted?** In calendar days from the termination notice date to the termination effective date, the notice date not counted.

## Cases (hypothetical dates)

| Termination effective date | Contract end date | Partial final month | Whole months | Notice lead | Months counted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 May 2026 | 31 December 2027 | yes | 19 | 75 days | 19 |
| 5 May 2026 | 31 December 2027 | yes | 19 | 40 days | 19.5 |
| 20 March 2026 | 10 January 2027 | yes | 9 | 60 days | 9 |
| 20 March 2026 | 10 January 2027 | yes | 9 | 59 days | 9.5 |
| 31 March 2026 | 31 December 2026 | no | 9 | any | 9 |
